dossier.architecture: Trapezoidal chassis built around enlarged coaxial DYE Rotor-family feeder and central turret.

subsystems.drivetrain: Front stock/rear custom-shaped X2S modules accommodate dish geometry; plate sides maximize rotor diameter.
subsystems.intake: Dual roller reduced to one to remove jams; compliant wheels replaced by continuous drum before Worlds.
subsystems.transfer: Eleven-position dish, coaxial independent hook/roller drive and doubled vertical roller sets clear central dead zone.
subsystems.scoring: Approximately 425-degree turret; third X44 added to main shooter for long passes/corner shots. Powered upper roller and compact ducking hood.
subsystems.endgame: Endgame installation not established in reviewed interview.
subsystems.controls: Shared robot-desire controls for auto/teleop; velocity/time-of-flight aiming, hub-state timing and configurable partner-compatible auto routes.

versions: Intake simplification and Worlds drum roller.
Two-to-three shooter-motor revision accompanied revised trajectory strategy.
dossier.analysis: The team explicitly traces the mechanism to its 2017 lineage, but the 2026 dish, coaxial drive, frame and singulation changes are substantial. The architecture chooses heading-independent scoring and adaptable roles over peak multi-lane output.
limits: Only the reviewed published configurations are established; intermediate changes may be undocumented.

context_documents.title: 2026-125 · Dish packaging and shooting independence require a coordinated robot
context_documents.body:
# 2026-125: Dish packaging and shooting independence require a coordinated robot

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The interview describes an eleven-position dish, front and rear vertical roller sets to clear its center, approximately 425 degrees of turret freedom, a 3-inch main shooter wheel, a 1-inch upper roller and additional feed wheels. A third X44 was added for difficult passes and corner shots. Intake and drivetrain packaging are shaped around the large dish.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team identifies moving shots, shooting under defense and simultaneous acquisition as reasons to retain the turret architecture. The doubled vertical rollers address fuel left in the dish center; the extra shooter motor addresses range/power demand.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

A centrally packaged turret is a whole-robot commitment. The dish determines where modules, structure and storage can sit, and its useful capacity depends on clearing the central dead region rather than nominal perimeter volume. Turret range is only useful if localization, target selection, hood travel and cable management support it. The FMS-aware timing offset is a flight-time decision: fuel released before activation must arrive while scoring is valid. That offset is not a transferable constant without checking release-to-arrival time and the applicable game timing.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare central residual fuel, sustained rate and moving-shot accuracy at different turret angles. Validate the hub-state lead time against measured flight time; verify cable/swept-volume clearance over the claimed angular range.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Kzn_t-LsDB8)

source_reviews.title: Team 125 NUTRONs interview
source_reviews.locator: 0:42–1:44 frame; 2:12–3:54 collector; 4:38–5:50 serializer; 5:52–7:34 turret; 9:22–12:59 controls and autonomous
source_reviews.review_basis: Read available English captions of the team interview. Times refer to the source video.
facts: Trapezoidal frame gives the dish space while leaving room for modules.
The team replaced a dual-roller intake with a continuous contact drum and revised the serializer center.
A rotating capture dish and central up-feed drive independently, with a low inset turret above.
source_reviews.limitations: Some reported values are configuration-specific. Captions do not authenticate event installation or hidden geometry.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: NUTRONs shaped the entire machine around the circular serializer. The chassis gives the moving capture mechanism a large footprint. Fuel exits the dish through the center, allowing one vertical path to supply the rotating shooter. This architecture buys freedom in where and when the robot can aim. It spends chassis volume, integration time and moving-shot tuning to get it. That makes it a useful rival for a wide fixed shooter, especially when evaluating whether aiming freedom pays for the feed and packaging cost.
piece_flow: The removable four-bar collector uses a continuous roller contact to pull fuel across the bumper.
Fuel settles into the enlarged circular working dish. The rotating pickup brings an intake point to pieces around the perimeter.
The independent center uptake captures fuel and carries it to the turret. Additional contacts close the dead region near the axis.
The turret sets yaw, the launcher establishes speed and the hood sets exit elevation. The hood has a low travel pose.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: The frame widens where the collector and dish need area and narrows toward the back. The interview describes a mix of stock and altered module packaging. A coaxial handoff reduces dependence on turret azimuth, but the rotating feeder, center column, wires, shooter sweep and access panels still need independent space. Keep the ground-to-dish and dish-to-column transitions serviceable after the superstructure is installed.

subsystems.name: Chassis around the dish
subsystems.construction: Wide front and tighter rear rails form a trapezoid around the circular fuel working volume. The rear modules are packaged around the dish.
subsystems.operation: Drive a low-profile route while leaving the center available for the serializer and launcher.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team selected the chassis shape to accommodate the enlarged dish.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Draw the actual dish working diameter and wheel envelopes before comparing frame shapes. Chassis corners that appear unused can still carry bumper mounts, wiring, battery access or collision loads.
subsystems.interfaces: Frame rails must support the dish and leave enough room for module extraction.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check whether a wheel or module can be replaced without disturbing dish alignment. Inspect rear mounts after side impacts.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact tolerances and installed mass distribution were not measured.

subsystems.name: Four-bar collector
subsystems.construction: Removable four-bar with a continuous roller and kicker geometry. The team describes a small set of shoulder bolts at the module interface.
subsystems.operation: Set the mouth low enough for fuel acquisition and carry fuel over the bumper into the dish.
subsystems.team_rationale: Earlier separated contact geometry jammed. The continuous roller reduces gaps in coverage.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A broad mouth can collect more fuel per approach, but weak coverage near supports can make one edge the practical bottleneck. An accessible removal joint limits the cost of impact repairs.
subsystems.interfaces: The extended mouth and retracting bars must clear the bumper and keep the low travel profile.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Compare edge pickup and simultaneous arrivals, then inspect the mount after offset contacts.
subsystems.unknowns: No measured approach tolerance or durability trials.

subsystems.name: Rotating capture and up-feed
subsystems.construction: A rotating dish and a separately driven central up-feed share an axis. Additional wheels address a center dead zone.
subsystems.operation: Move the pickup point to fuel around the dish and lift it in a single stream to the turret.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team kept the serializer for moving-shot flexibility and made the working dish larger.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Independent speeds let the mechanism tune capture availability separately from the upward feed. A jam at the central intake can still starve a ready launcher.
subsystems.interfaces: The center outlet must deliver consistent piece position across dish orientations and turret motion.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Measure recovery from two pieces entering together and the fraction of fuel stranded near the center.
subsystems.unknowns: Team-reported working dish counts are configuration estimates. Bulk hopper capacity is a different quantity.

subsystems.name: Turret, hood and moving shot
subsystems.construction: Inset yaw drive, multi-motor launcher and lowering hood. The team discusses interpolation and motion compensation.
subsystems.operation: Select range-based settings, move to target yaw and adjust the shot for the robot’s motion and flight time.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team chose the architecture to score or feed while moving around defense.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Compare the fraction of usable field time when the robot can collect and shoot with an alternative that turns the chassis. The value of yaw freedom depends on maintained localization, shot readiness and a reliable single feed.
subsystems.interfaces: Hood lowering determines trench travel clearance. Cable limits constrain turret travel and where the scoring pose can resume.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Verify a missed camera update, a shot at a yaw limit and recovery after multiple fuel loads.
subsystems.unknowns: No independent accuracy map or matched comparison with a fixed shooter.

revisions: Dual collector arrangement changed to a continuous roller.
Central uptake contacts and launcher power were revised.
transferable_principles: Lay out the feeder, frame and drive modules together when a large round component sets the envelope.
Compare shooting flexibility against the number of pieces delivered and scored per whole cycle.
Use a constrained test to separate a poor center handoff from a slow launch mechanism.
disconfirming_conditions: A fixed wide shooter can win where the scoring route naturally provides the required heading and full-bin throughput matters more.
A rotating shooter can earn its complexity when usable moving shots preserve collection routes and reduce defender control.
remaining_gaps: Configuration-by-event mapping, complete mechanical dimensions, measured workload, accuracy and scoring-rate distributions.
